title: Request filament weave and priority maps
content:
TL;DR
This doc stitches together ~40 small-to-medium customer asks collected between 2026-05 and 2026-07 into a set of 'filaments' (related request threads) and proposes a compact priority map for Q3 probe work. Goal: identify 3 low-effort, high-impact interventions we can ship as micro-patches and 2 mid-term bets to feed into Product backlog grooming.

Why this format?
- We keep seeing related micro-asks that individually look minor but together show consistent friction patterns (prefix caching surprises, token billing confusion, model fallback mismatches).
- A filament approach groups items by common root cause rather than feature ask name. Easier to propose single-stop fixes.

Methodology / data sources
- Source: customer support threads, CSM field notes, community forum snippets, and two recorded calls (Acct A, Acct B) dated 2026-06.
- Heuristic grouping: similarity by problem symptom (latency spike, wrong fallback choice, billing surprise, embedding drift), then manual curation.
- Priority scoring: frequency (1–5), customer impact (1–5), implementation effort estimate (S/M/L).

Filaments (summarized)
1) Prefix cache confusion (freq 17, impact 4) — customers assume cached prefixes persist across model variants; chaos when we route to quantized models
   - Representative asks: “Why did my long-context prompt suddenly cost 3x?”; “Responses are truncated after switching region.”
   - Quick fix candidates: surface a short inline banner in Console per-route: “Routing to variant X — prefix cache not shared”; update API error message when fallback occurs.
   - Effort: small (console + message tweak).

2) Fallback model mismatch (freq 13, impact 5) — automated fallback picks different temperature/penalty defaults, producing unexpected outputs
   - Asks: requests to expose fallback policy and allow user overrides per-route; desire for a preview/dry-run mode of fallback behavior
   - Proposal: add ‘fallback-preview’ API param that simulates route decisions and returns a decision trace (no tokens consumed).
   - Effort: medium (runtime + API contract), high product value.

3) Embedding consistency & version tagging (freq 11, impact 4) — downstream indexers break when we silently rotate embedding hash/normalization
   - Asks: stable embedding metadata, semantic version in response headers, migration guide for indexers
   - Quick fix: add header X-embed-version and a changelog entry; mid-term: embed-version pinning for dedicated customers.
   - Effort: small-to-medium.

4) Cost/Quota transparency (freq 9, impact 5) — users surprised by per-token rounding and ephemeral short bursts that drain quota
   - Asks: per-request estimated token delta before execution; per-route rolling-24h burn view; auto-notify when a single request exceeds threshold
   - Proposal: console preview cost estimator + backend estimated_token_count flag returned in request metadata.
   - Effort: medium but aligns with billing roadmap.

5) Dev ergonomics: local dev -> private deploy path friction (freq 7, impact 3)
   - Asks: reference config snippets for Docker Compose for private runtimes; a short checklist for KMS setup quirks
   - Quick fix: one-pager + repo sample; Effort: small.

Representative customer quotes (raw)
- “We’re seeing an abrupt drop in reply quality after the fallback — it’s like switching from jazz to a lecture.” — Acct B, fintech
- “My quota vanished during a load test and billing support said it was token rounding — that felt… unfair.” — Acct Q, marketplace
- “If we can pin embeddings per-run, we won’t have to re-index every week.” — Acct L, content search startup

Micro-patch candidates (ship within 2–4 sprints)
- Console prefix-cache banner and per-route fallback annotation (owner: Console eng; tickets: JIRA:CS-3912)
- Add X-embed-version response header and changelog stub (owner: Serving-runtime; ticket: CS-3925)
- Quick 'cost preview' toggle in Console (UI only MVP that calls estimator endpoint)

Mid-term bets (Q4 backlog candidates)
- Fallback-preview API param + decision trace (costly but reduces surprise, also useful for SRE debugging)
- Per-request estimated_token_count returned before generation (aligns with billing and quota UX)

Open questions / risks
- Privacy: how much decision trace detail can we return without exposing model internals? (legal/security check required)
- Metrics: we need a baseline metric to measure 'surprise reduction' — propose: % of escalations mentioning fallback or billing surprise in CS tickets per week.
- Engineering capacity: Serving-runtime already has two medium projects; add estimate to roadmap grooming.

Next steps (actionable)
- This week: triage micro-patch candidates in RFC channel and assign owners (Maya to ping Console + Serving leads).
- By 2026-08-09: prototype console prefix banner and X-embed-version header; demo to CS + Solutions Eng.
- Gather 2–3 customers for pilot of fallback-preview API (ask: Rafael to recruit).

Appendix: selective tickets & refs (copy/paste friendly)
- JIRA CS-3912 — console: route annotations + cache banner (owner: Alex W)
- JIRA CS-3925 — runtime: embed-version header (owner: Priya N)
- Confluence: CS-8897 — fallbacks design notes
- Slack: #cs-voice-thread-07-15 — raw thread with 9 customer quotes

Quick notes / field scribbles (raw, unedited)
- ask: allow route-level fallback override? maybe dangerous — could create SLA loopholes.
- on billing preview: need to be conservative; estimator must provide upper-bound so customers are never under-informed.
- potential PR: small doc + sample curl: `GET /v1/route/preview?prompt=...` returns token_estimate header.

Questions for Product review meeting
- Do we prioritize billing transparency (user trust) vs fallback-preview (developer control)? Which reduces churn more?
- What guardrails for fallback-preview (rate-limits, info exposure)?

End notes
- This is intentionally rough — meant as a field-synthesis input to Product backlog grooming. Please annotate inline or add comments in Confluence patch CS-8897.
- If you want a condensed 1-page exec blurb, I can produce a 1-slide version highlighting the three micro-patches and two mid-term bets.

TODOs
- [ ] Maya: open RFC in product-hosted-api with this filament grouping (due 2026-07-22)
- [ ] Rafael: recruit pilot customers for fallback-preview (due 2026-07-30)
- [ ] Priya: quick patch for embed-version header (PR target 2026-07-29)
